messages.content:
You review lifestyle plans written by FOXO's lifestyle coach for a member in India.

You will see the member's profile, the abnormal results the plan targets, and the full plan. Judge whether a member could act on the plan tomorrow. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- specific: Recommendations give concrete foods with portions or timing, not generic advice like "eat healthy".
- practical: The foods are everyday Indian foods a member could easily buy and cook.
- explained: Each recommendation says how it helps the linked biomarker.
- activity_concrete: The activity advice says what to do, for how long and how often.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Diet: jain. Allergies: peanut. Conditions: type 2 diabetes.
Abnormal results: hba1c 7.1 % (high), ldl 140.0 mg/dL (high)

Plan:
Focus areas: Improve HbA1c with fixed meal timings and controlled carbohydrate portions; Lower LDL with soluble fiber and reduced fried/full-fat foods; Keep all meals Jain-friendly: no onion, garlic, root vegetables or honey; Keep all foods peanut-free due to allergy
Foods to eat:
- At breakfast, eat 2 medium moong dal chillas with 1 cup cooked spinach and 1 small bowl of mint-coriander chutney (no onion/garlic), or 1 small bowl (30 g dry) steel-cut oats cooked in water with 1/2 cup diced apple and no honey or sugar. (why: A protein-and-fiber breakfast with whole grains or dal helps slow blood-sugar rise and supports better HbA1c control.; linked to hba1c)
- At lunch, use a plate method: 1/2 plate non-root seasonal sabzi and salad (gourd, beans, spinach, cabbage, capsicum, cucumber, tomato), 1/4 plate 1 katori (150 g cooked) toor or moong dal, and 1/4 plate 2 small jowar or bajra rotis or 1 cup cooked millet rice. Avoid onion, garlic and root vegetables. (why: High-fiber dal, millets and non-root vegetables lower the glycemic load of the meal and support HbA1c reduction.; linked to hba1c)
- At 4–5 pm, eat 30 g roasted chana or 1 small bowl (100 g) moong sprouts chaat with lemon, coriander and cucumber; do not add onion, garlic or peanuts. (why: A measured high-fiber, protein snack reduces hunger and helps avoid sweet or fried evening foods that raise blood sugar.; linked to hba1c)
- Finish dinner by 7:30–8 pm: 1 cup cooked foxtail or bajra millet khichdi with 1/2 cup moong dal and 1 cup non-root vegetables such as lauki, tinda, beans or palak; or 2 bajra rotis with 1 katori palak dal and 1 katori cabbage sabzi. (why: An early, portion-controlled dinner with millets and dal improves overnight blood-sugar control and supports HbA1c.; linked to hba1c)
- Include one soluble-fiber food daily: 1 medium guava or apple, 1 cup cooked oats, 1 katori cooked okra (bhindi), or 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed mixed into curd or vegetables. (why: Soluble fiber helps bind cholesterol in the gut and supports LDL reduction; fruit portions are kept small for diabetes.; linked to ldl)
- For cooking and toppings, keep total oil to about 3 teaspoons per day (mustard, rice bran or olive oil), choose steamed/boiled/grilled foods, and if your doctor agrees, use only 1 small handful (15 g) unsalted almonds or walnuts as a snack. (why: Reducing total fat and replacing fried foods with measured healthy fats helps lower LDL while keeping calories controlled.; linked to ldl)
Foods to limit or avoid: Sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets, mithai, sweetened drinks, fruit juices and sherbets; Peanuts/groundnuts and any food containing them, including peanut chutney, peanut oil and groundnut sweets; Onion, garlic, and root vegetables such as potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar (Jain diet); Deep-fried and high-fat foods: puri, samosa, pakora, vada, chips, biscuits, white bread, maida naan and bakery items; Full-fat paneer, butter, ghee and cream in large amounts; use only small measured portions if at all; Meat, fish, seafood and eggs (Jain diet)
Activity: Follow your doctor's advice. As no exercise restriction is noted, aim for a 15–20 minute easy walk after meals, building to 30 minutes of brisk walking on most days; add light bodyweight exercise 2 days a week only if your doctor agrees. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or breathlessness.
Sleep: Aim for 7–8 hours nightly with fixed sleep and wake times; finish dinner by 7:30–8 pm, avoid screens for 1 hour before bed, and avoid heavy late-night meals.
Retest in 12 weeks

Nothing is left as generic advice.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "practical", "reasoning": "The foods are standard Indian staples — moong/toor dal, chillas, jowar/bajra rotis, millet khichdi, lauki, tinda, palak, bhindi, roasted chana, guava, curd, mustard oil — all easy to buy and cook anywhere in India, and all consistent with Jain restrictions and the peanut allergy.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "explained", "reasoning": "Each food recommendation carries an explicit 'why' statement tied to a biomarker: protein-and-fiber breakfast and high-fiber dal/millets slow blood-sugar rise for HbA1c, while soluble fiber binds cholesterol in the gut and reduced fried/full-fat foods with measured healthy fats for LDL.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "activity_concrete", "reasoning": "The activity advice specifies what to do (easy walk after meals, building to brisk walking, plus light bodyweight exercise), how long (15–20 minutes building to 30 minutes), and how often (after meals, most days, 2 days per week), with clear safety stop signs.", "passed": true}]}
